chunks: From him, from Ja'far, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him say: 'Pre-emption (al-shuf'ah) is not valid except for a partner.'

key_terms.الشُّفْعَةُ: Pre-emption (right of first refusal in property sales)

ai.seo_question: Who is entitled to the right of pre-emption in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) is strictly limited to co-owners, excluding single owners or unrelated third parties. This distinction is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for resolving disputes over shared real estate, ensuring that a partner has the first right to acquire the sold share to preserve the integrity of the co-ownership structure.
